summary.text: This briefing explores combining Gaussian processes and principal component-based dimensionality reduction for uncertainty quantification in complex physical systems. By compressing high-dimensional responses using principal components, probabilistic surrogate models can efficiently estimate epistemic and aleatoric uncertainties. This combination addresses computational bottlenecks when modeling high-dimensional or time-dependent experimental and simulation data.

target_user.text: The target user includes researchers and engineers developing surrogate models for complex physical systems, as indicated by the repository and package usage in uncertainty quantification, chemistry, and language-agent frameworks.

jtbd.text: Perform efficient uncertainty quantification on high-dimensional simulation or experimental outputs by reducing dimensionality before applying probabilistic surrogate models.

value_prop.text: Reduces the computational cost of modeling high-dimensional spatial or temporal responses while preserving valid uncertainty estimates and physical consistency.

riskiest_assumption.text: The riskiest assumption is viability (axis V), which was designated due to missing evidence in the bundle. We assume that enterprise customers are willing to pay for a specialized dimensionality-reduction and Gaussian process uncertainty quantification tool rather than relying on custom internal scripts.

mvp.text: Run customer interviews and price acceptance tests with simulation engineers to evaluate willingness to pay for a combined dimensionality-reduction and Gaussian process uncertainty quantification workflow, targeting a proposed threshold of 30 percent conversion for paid pilot interest.
mvp.type: customer interviews and price acceptance test

success_metric.text: Achieve a proposed threshold of at least 40 percent of interviewed engineering teams confirming that the tool solves a critical high-dimensional uncertainty bottleneck, alongside a positive price acceptance test at a proposed threshold of 500 dollars per month.

kill_criteria.text: Fewer than a proposed threshold of 10 percent of prospective users express willingness to pay during price acceptance testing.
Feedback indicates that existing in-house dimensionality reduction scripts are considered entirely sufficient, preventing commercial adoption below a proposed threshold of 20 percent market interest.

open_source.use: Provides high-quality implementations of baseline methods for uncertainty tasks.
Supplies Gaussian process emulator packages for complex systems.
Offers geometric kernels for structured representations.

to_build.text: A unified pipeline integrating principal component extraction with Gaussian process surrogate training and calibration.
